findings.body: The `None` arm of `shorten` fires when the first `limit` characters contain no space — e.g. a long compound word or CJK text with no spaces. None of the four tests reach it: the Japanese fixture is only 17 characters so it hits the early return, and the other two multibyte fixtures contain spaces. This branch also returns `limit + 1` characters (`head` is `limit` chars plus the 1-char ellipsis), which exceeds the documented "at most `limit` characters" contract — a test that asserts `shorten("AVeryLongWordWithoutSpaces", 10).chars().count() <= 10` would fail today. The repo rules require at least 80% coverage of meaningful behaviour; this is a meaningful, reachable branch with zero coverage.
findings.title: Test the no-space branch of shorten

findings.body: The `None` arm of `first_sentence` fires when the text has no ". " sequence — a single sentence, a sentence ending with a period but no trailing space, or text with no sentence punctuation. The only `first_sentence` test asserts the `Some` branch. The repo rules require at least 80% coverage of meaningful behaviour; this fallback branch handles a common case and is untested.
findings.title: Test the no-delimiter branch of first_sentence

value.summary: The change adds a `summarise` module with truncation helpers, a MongoDB kernel-bypass dev shim, and compose/env wiring fixes. The `summarise.rs` tests pin the happy paths but leave both `None` branches unexercised; the `shorten` `None` branch also returns `limit + 1` characters, exceeding the documented ceiling. No lookups needed — the functions are self-contained in the diff.
